Issue: Chapter detection never reports which method it used, so a wrong count is silent

## Summary

`detect_structure()` picks between two ways of counting chapters and prints nothing about the choice:

```python
chapters_detected = (
    numeric_count if numeric_count > 0 else _structural_chapter_count(text)
)
```

The number lands in `metadata.json` and in the run output with no indication of which method produced it, at which heading depth, or what the other method saw. When the count is wrong, nothing in the output says so.

## Why this is the shape of a defect and not a nice-to-have

Every parser in this codebase already reports its decisions:

```
Trying python-docx... OK
Trying stdlib DOCX parser... OK
  [warn] extract_with_pdftotext failed: …
  [security] removed 3 invisible Unicode code point(s) from book.pdf
```

Same class of decision — method A or method B, with a fallback — and five loud paths sit next to one silent one. This is an inconsistency inside the project's own convention, not a new feature request.

The cost is concrete. In a real conversion of a 26-page paper with 8 numbered sections (#143), the run reported 4 chapters. The user only discovered it by reading the headings themselves; nothing in the output invited suspicion. And `chapters_detected` is not cosmetic — Step 3 plans from it and the generated skill's file layout follows it, so a wrong count silently becomes the structure of the artifact.

Of the frictions from that session, this is the only one with no floor under it: a false scanner alert stops the run visibly, a missing-dependency message is annoying but the fallback still produces output, and a wrong chapter count produces a confident, complete-looking, wrong skill.

## Suggested change

One line, in the convention already used elsewhere:

```
Chapters: 8 (structural, depth 2)
Chapters: 12 (numeric)
Chapters: 1 (structural, depth 1) — only one heading level found
```

Worth considering alongside it:

- record the method in `metadata.json` next to `chapters_detected`, so a batch run can be audited afterwards rather than watched live;
- when the structural fallback returns 0 or 1 on a document of non-trivial length, say so explicitly — that combination is nearly always a detection failure rather than a one-chapter book.

## Not in scope

The heuristic itself is #143. This issue is only about the run being able to tell you which answer you got and how it was reached.
